title: Leader personality profile: private, Big Five, two lengths
description: A Big Five personality profile for leaders: a 20-question quick test or a 120-question full test. Private to you until you choose to share it.
lead: A personality profile built on the Big Five, from the public-domain IPIP items. Take the quick test of 20 questions or the full test of 120. The result is yours alone, until you choose to share it with your group.
summary: A private Big Five profile, shared only if you choose.

items.title: Know your own tendencies
points: Five domains, each placed lower, middle or higher on the answer scale.
Never good or bad: a trait describes you.
Private by default, and yours to delete at once.

items.title: Understand each other better
points: Each member shares at the level they choose, or not at all.
People lists what each member has shared, and nothing more.
A starting point for talking about how you work together.

items.title: Development, never selection
points: It is for each leader’s own development.
It is never used for selection, promotion or performance evaluation.
No admin or coach has a path to anyone’s profile.

blocks.title: Two lengths
blocks.text: The quick test asks 20 questions and is labelled a first look. The full test asks 120, with the five domains and their facets. Both use the published IPIP items, word for word.
points: Progress is saved, so you can stop and come back.
Your answers are not stored: only the sums the result needs.
blocks.alt: The quick test on a phone: question 1 of 20, “Am the life of the party.”, with Moderately accurate chosen.
blocks.caption: The quick test’s first question.

blocks.title: Your result, on Me
blocks.text: Each domain is shown as lower, middle or higher on the answer scale, with your own position marked. No norm group is used yet, and the page says so.
points: You choose what each group sees: nothing, domains, or domains and facets.
A retake replaces the profile and resets sharing to nothing.
blocks.alt: The Leader Profile on Me: five domains with a band and a dot each. What the group sees is set to domains.
blocks.caption: A quick test result, shared with the group as domains.

blocks.title: What the group sees
blocks.text: People lists each member and what they have shared. A profile that is not shared reads “Not shared”, the same as no profile, so no one can tell whether one exists.
blocks.alt: People: eight members; Kari Nordmann shares five domains as bands, and the others read Not shared.
blocks.caption: People, with one profile shared as domains.

items.title: Nothing
items.text: Your profile shows as Not shared. This is where every profile starts.

items.title: Domains
items.text: The five domains, as lower, middle or higher. No facets.

items.title: Domains and facets
items.text: The five domains and their facets, as lower, middle or higher.

blocks.title: Never a judgement
blocks.text: The profile describes tendencies. It shows no trait as good or bad, and a group sees only a band, never a number. It is for development, never for selection, promotion or performance evaluation.

faq.q: Where do the questions come from?
faq.a: From the International Personality Item Pool, which is in the public domain. The quick test is the Mini-IPIP and the full test is the IPIP-NEO-120, both word for word.
Only you, until you share it with a group. You choose the level for each group, and it applies at once.
Yes. Deleting removes the profile and every share at once. It cannot be undone.

faq.q: Is it compared with other leaders?
faq.a: Not yet. Results are placed on the answer scale in three equal bands, and the page says that no norm group is used.
